description: When a lesson presents complex material as a continuous, transient stream (a narrated animation, a video, a live demonstration) to learners for whom its steps are new, presenting it in meaningful segments with a pause or a continue control between them is expected to improve retention and transfer over one continuous presentation, at the cost of more learning time; meta-analyses test this, and it holds when the system sets the pauses, matters more for complex than for simple material, and its relation to prior knowledge is mixed.
title: Segmenting Principle

description: For learners who expect an evaluation to confirm a negative judgement of their group or of them, a 10–15 minute private essay on a personally important value, given to the whole class before the threat, is expected to protect later grades compared with writing about an unimportant value; one claim tests this, with two positive small field experiments and a null large replication, so effects are small and unpredictable.
title: Self Affirmation

description: Handing a learner decisions about goals, resources, pace, strategy and evaluation is expected to sustain engagement and build independence without costing learning only when the learner knows enough about the content to choose well, has been taught to plan, monitor and evaluate in the subject, and is given control gradually with checked checkpoints; no claim in the wiki compares learner-directed with teacher-directed study directly.
title: Self-Directed Learning

description: For a learner with a readable criterion and a next move for each result, taught, test-based checks of their own work at set points during a task are expected to improve performance on it, but no claim here isolates self-monitoring against its absence on a learning outcome.
title: Self-monitoring

description: When learners are explicitly taught and prompted to plan, monitor against stated criteria and act on what they notice, their regulation activity and task performance may improve, qualified by monitoring accuracy, prior knowledge, whether support is used, and which outcome is measured.
title: Self-Regulated Learning

description: For a novice on a target whose parts depend on each other, meeting the parts in an order that puts what a step rests on before it and moves from what the learner can process toward full complexity, revised from the learner's responses, is expected to improve performance on tasks that draw on the whole; no claim tests that general rule, and tests of particular orders (example or problem first, parts or whole first, blocked or mixed) favour different orders for different learners and goals.
title: Sequencing
